ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=4\mathrm{kg}$ is at rest on an inclined plane under the action of a horizontal constant force $F=26\mathrm{N}$. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the normal force exerted by the inclined plane on the object?
2. What is the frictional force acting on the object?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$47.6\mathrm{N}$
$3.2\mathrm{N}$, direction upward along the inclined plane

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=4\mathrm{kg}$ is at rest on an inclined plane under the action of a horizontal constant force $F=26\mathrm{N}$. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$. 1. What is the magnitude of the normal force exerted by the inclined plane on the object? 2. What is the frictional force acting on the object?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $47.6\mathrm{N}$ $3.2\mathrm{N}$, direction upward along the inclined plane
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: the block m is located on an inclined plane sloping upward to the right, and the inclination angle of the inclined plane is θ=37°; the block is subjected to a constant horizontal force F=26 N to the right, and the block is in a stationary state. Perform force analysis: gravity mg is vertically downward, the horizontal force F is to the right, the normal force N is perpendicular to the inclined plane and outward, and the static friction force f is along the direction of the inclined plane. Take coordinate axes perpendicular to the inclined plane and parallel to the inclined plane. Equilibrium in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane: the component of the horizontal force F perpendicular to the inclined plane presses the block toward the inclined plane, with magnitude F sin37°; the component of gravity perpendicular to the inclined plane also presses toward the inclined plane, with magnitude mg cos37°. Therefore N = mg cos37° + F sin37°. Substitute m=4 kg, g≈10 m/s², sin37°≈0.6, cos37°≈0.8: N = 40×0.8 + 26×0.6 = 32 + 15.6 = 47.6 N. Direction parallel to the inclined plane: the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin37° = 40×0.6 = 24 N; the component of the horizontal pushing force upward along the inclined plane is F cos37° = 26×0.8 = 20.8 N. Since 24 N > 20.8 N, the block has a tendency to move downward along the inclined plane, so the static friction force is upward along the inclined plane. Static equilibrium requires f = 24 - 20.8 = 3.2 N.
